name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 district partisan lean in West Virginia
Incumbent Riley Moore with a large fundraising advantage
Challenger Ace Parsi raised only about $134k with no outside spending
Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 3%
model.rationale: The R+20 lean, Moore's incumbency, and his roughly ten-to-one cash advantage over Parsi leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, and markets agree at about 97% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings to the contrary, the forecast stays at a wide Republican margin.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Parsi within single digits, or major outside spending entering the district, would be the first sign this is closer than priced.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Riley Moore, the Republican incumbent, seeks a second term in a West Virginia district that leans about twenty points Republican at the presidential level. His challenger, Democrat Ace Parsi, has raised roughly $134,000 and had about $44,000 on hand, while Moore has raised about $1.3 million and holds more than $750,000 in cash. No outside groups have spent meaningfully against Moore.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, and prediction markets put Moore's chances near 97%. The district's strong Republican tilt and the incumbent's financial edge make an upset unlikely; the forecast calls the race Safe Republican with a wide expected margin.
